questions.q: What single real change turns the vulnerable withdraw function into the fixed version?
options: Renaming the function
Removing the require statement entirely
Resetting the balance to zero before making the external call, instead of after
Adding a pragma version bump
questions.explain: The only real change is moving the balance reset earlier — from after the .call to before it — following the checks-effects-interactions order.

questions.q: What is the real, correct order of the checks-effects-interactions pattern?
options: There is no real fixed order — any order works equally well
Interactions, then checks, then effects
Effects, then interactions, then checks
Checks, then effects (state changes), then interactions (external calls)
questions.explain: First verify conditions (checks), then update your own state (effects), and only then make external calls (interactions) — this exact order is what prevents reentrancy.

questions.q: How does the real `noReentrant` modifier actually stop a reentrancy attack?
options: It requires a password to call the function
It deletes the function entirely
It only works if the attacker uses a different account
It sets a locked boolean to true while the function runs, so a nested re-entry call fails the require(!locked) check
questions.explain: The modifier locks the contract for the duration of the function call — if the attacker's fallback tries to re-enter, locked is already true, and the check fails.

questions.q: Per the instructor's real, honest advice, what do most production contracts actually use for reentrancy protection?
options: Only the checks-effects-interactions pattern, never a guard modifier
No protection at all — reentrancy is considered unavoidable
A completely different, undisclosed technique
OpenZeppelin's audited ReentrancyGuard, rather than a hand-written version
questions.explain: The instructor noted that popular real projects overwhelmingly use OpenZeppelin's own ReentrancyGuard rather than writing their own from scratch.

questions.q: Why are checks-effects-interactions and the reentrancy guard described as independent defenses?
options: A contract could use either one alone and still be protected from the same real exploit built in the previous lesson
They must always be used together or neither works
Checks-effects-interactions only works on testnets
The guard modifier replaces the need for a withdraw function entirely
questions.explain: Either fix on its own neutralizes the specific reentrancy exploit demonstrated earlier — correct state ordering, or a lock preventing re-entry, both independently close the same door.
